newsitem.title: USA: Raleigh, N.C., group abandons hockey bid.
newsitem.headline: Raleigh, N.C., group abandons hockey bid.

text.p: North Carolina's Centennial Authority, which was formed to help finance a new arena in Raleigh, said it regrets the decision by a local group to withdraw its bid for a National Hockey League franchise.
In a prepared statement Tuesday, the authority said, "We believe now as we have always that major league hockey would have succeeded in the arena."
Triangle Professional Ice Hockey Inc, headed by Charlotte Businessman Feliz Sabates withdrew his bid for an NHL team during the holiday weekend.

Sabates had been strongly critical of local officials. In a letter a letter to authority Chairman Steve Stroud, Sabates accused the authority of misinformation and misrepresentation during the negotiations, which he referred to as "a charade."

The NHL team, if awarded, would have played at a $120 million arena that the Centennial Authority is building for North Carolina State University, under a funding agreement with the City of Raleigh and Wake County.

The authority said in its statement that the group had done everything in its power to work with Sabates mand that, "We regret that the Triangle Professional Ice Hockey, Inc. came to this conclusion."
